title: Power BI Pricing in 2026 and What Each License Costs
summary: Power BI pricing ranges from free to build, per-user fees to share, and $263/month for dedicated capacity. Choose the tier that fits your needs.
body_markdown:
## Ways to Lower a Power BI Bill


Work through these six fixes in order, because each one saves more than the one after it and most need nothing more than an afternoon with your admin settings.


Each fix ends with a check.


Downgrade unused Pro seats. Every paid seat nobody opens is money wasted monthly.


Pull the usage report from the admin portal and list people with no activity in recent months. Check: the paid-seat count in your Microsoft 365 admin centre drops by the number you removed.


**Split creators from viewers** . Most people in a company read reports and never build one, yet they often carry the same licence as the analysts.


Give the paid tier only to those who publish, and move the rest to a cheaper route. Check: compare the list of people who published anything against the list of people who hold a paid seat.


### Capacity, bundles and duplicate data


Move wide distribution to capacity. Once a report reaches a large audience, paying per reader costs more than renting shared computing power, which lets free-licence viewers open it.


Check: price both routes for your actual viewer count before you commit.


Right-size Fabric. Fabric is Microsoft's bundled data platform, and its capacity bills whether anyone is using it or not. If it sits idle overnight and at weekends, you're paying for empty rooms.


Pause it when idle or drop to a smaller size. Check: the capacity metrics app shows peak load well under what you bought.


Check your Microsoft 365 bundles. Some existing Microsoft plans already include Power BI rights, so you may be paying twice. Check: match each paid seat against the plan that person already holds.


Remove duplicate datasets. Copies of the same data each refresh and consume capacity, and people trust the wrong one. Check: search the workspace for datasets sharing a source and see which still have readers.
